name: From Katana to Camcorder: Japan's Road to Power
description: Warlords and poets, shoguns and artists, a country that closed its doors, opened them, fell in war and rebuilt itself into a world leader.

checkpoints.name: Court and warriors
checkpoints.note: Shinto shrines and the Heian court in Kyoto produced The Tale of Genji by Murasaki Shikibu. Meanwhile provincial warriors, the samurai, carried long curved swords and bows and gained power.

checkpoints.name: Rule of the warrior
checkpoints.note: Shoguns ruled in place of emperors. Samurai drove back the Mongol invasions of 1274 and 1281, Nichiren preached a new Buddhism, and Noh theatre took form.

checkpoints.name: The country at war
checkpoints.note: In the Sengoku period lords fought each other. Oda Nobunaga broke his rivals, Tokugawa Ieyasu won the last war, and castles such as Himeji were raised.

checkpoints.name: Peace under the Tokugawa
checkpoints.note: The Tokugawa shogunate kept the peace and closed Japan. In Edo, kabuki, Basho's poems and ukiyo-e flourished, and Hokusai made The Great Wave before Perry's ships arrived.

checkpoints.name: Meiji, empire and war
checkpoints.note: The Meiji Restoration brought a new constitution, fast industrial growth and a victory over Russia, and firms such as Toyota grew from it later. The Empire of Japan then went to war and was defeated after Pearl Harbor, Midway and Hiroshima.

checkpoints.name: Japan rebuilt
checkpoints.note: Postwar Japan produced Kurosawa's Seven Samurai, Sony, the Shinkansen bullet train and Studio Ghibli, until the bubble economy burst around 1991 and a long slow period began.
